text:
audit-bot: ALERT: us-east-1 GPU fleet: rising boot failures (12%) and repeated STS/KMS denies since 05:40 UTC. Investigating.

alex: I see `AccessDenied` on kms:Decrypt for boot key and STS AssumeRole denies for gpu-bootstrap-role. This started right after a small NAT/egress optimization push.
priya: traces show pv-provisioner calls assumeRole then immediately calls keystore via vpce. CloudTrail shows vpce id vpce-9a7 but our KMS policy was switched to check `aws:SourceVpc` only in today's PR. VPCE->VPC mapping drifted during a host migration.
mike: also audit events were missing for ~8m because the shipper couldn't reach s3; egress rule tightened in the same change window. logs are delayed forensics is hard.
ops-runbook-bot: suggested quick steps: 1) apply a canary KMS policy override to allow gpu-bootstrap-role for Decrypt, 2) open audit egress from privatelink subnets, 3) temporarily reduce warm-pool desired capacity by 25% to limit retry storm costs.
priya: doing canary now on 5% of the warm pool. snippet: `aws kms put-key-policy --key-id bootkey-3 --policy file://canary-allow.json` which loosens the SourceVpc condition.
audit-bot: audit egress rule reopened; CloudTrail/shipper events are streaming back. Found CT entries where sourceVpc is vpc-old-12 while vpce maps to a new-vpc id.
alex: canary results: boot failure in slice dropped from 12% -> 1.6% within 70s. joins latency improved from ~2.1s -> 430ms. One AZ still shows intermittent conntrack_exhausted spikes.
mike: I pinned collector uploads to a dedicated ENI to reduce ephemeral port usage; conntrack metrics stabilized.
ops-runbook-bot: recommendation: proceed controlled rollout 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% with 5m observation windows and keep warm-pool scaled down until stable. Also create follow-up: replace SourceVpc condition with `aws:VpcEndpointId` in KMS policies and add PR smoke-test for VPCE mapping.
priya: filing INFRA-517: keystore-vpce-mapping-and-audit-egress. tagging @sre-finance for estimated surge ~+$3.2k/day if warm-pool remains inflated.
alex: thanks. will keep thread pinned and post postmortem summary once stable.
